description.narrative: In January-March 2022, a Rapid assessment of the situation of workers in the informal economy, identifying gaps in accessing social protection schemes has been carried out. Its results, conclusions and recommendations have been validated by the National Tripartite Commission in July 2022. The objective of the exercise was to identify the impact of COVID-19 on informal workers and their families as well as developments in the post COVID-19 recovery period. It seeks to give voice to women and men who depend on the informal economy so that their situation is taken into account in the development of employment, social protection and formalization policies. The survey also aimed to better understand the diversity of their situations and perceptions about trust in and accountability of institutions. The Tripartite Commission decided to use the results from the Rapid assessment to guide the design of the new Strategy and Action Plan for the Reduction of Informal Employment as the current one expires end of 2023. Based on the findings of the rapid assessment, the Federation of Independent Trade Unions of Tajikistan (FITUT) developed its Strategy and Action Plan on formalization through extending its services to informal workers, dependent self-employed and those in non-standard forms of employment. The new Strategy and Action Plan were developed in April-July 2022 and cover the period of 2022-2026. The new Strategy and Action Plan encompass all sectors and, in a way, replaces the previous Strategy of the FITUT designed for the promotion of formalization specifically for the agriculture sector. The draft Strategy and Action Plan have been widely discussed in the series of validation meetings conducted in all regions and major towns in the period of August-October 2022. The Strategy and the Action Plan have been validated and finally adopted by the General Council of the FITUT in October 2022. The Rapid assessment with informal workers on their socio-economic situation, social protection coverage and affiliation with trade unions that was conducted during January-April 2022 based on the methodology developed by and with the support of the ILO in partnership with the Ministry of Labour, Migration and Employment, the Federation of Trade Union of Tajikistan, and the Union of Employers of Tajikistan. A series of trainings for the leaders and activists of the Federation of Independent Trade Union in Tajikistan (FITUT) were conducted during April-September 2022 that helped to build the capacity of trade unions to reach out to informal workers, support them towards self-organising and becoming union members, present options for formalisation of their employment relations and benefits of joining social insurance schemes. With the contribution of RBSA, the ILO provided technical inputs to the development of the Strategy and Action Plan on Formalization.

description.narrative: The National Strategy for Social Protection (NSSP) until 2040 was adopted by the Government in December 2022. It sets three main policy priorities for the social protection sector: (i) institutional modernization of the social protection system, (ii) ensuring long-term sustainability of the pension system and (iii) adopting additional protective and incentivizing measures to expand social protection coverage. The NSSP was developed by the National Tripartite Committee on Decent Work (NTCDC). It is also a result of the ILO and UNCT's 2018 Assessment Based National Dialogue for the Social Protection System and direct technical inputs and consultations with the Ministry of Health and Social Protection between March and October 2022 during the various drafting stages of the NSSP and background documents validated by constituents, the findings of which are included in the NSSP. ILO support to constituents included background analysis, technical inputs, and capacity development for key staff of the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, Ministry of Labour, Migration and Employment, Agency for Social Protection and Public Employment Services. ILO provided technical support to the NTCDC in the drafting of the NSSP and the National Productive Employment Programme 2023-2027 approved on 28 May 2022 which, among other key issues addresses the need to extend social insurance and measures supporting the transition from the informal to formal economy. Key support interventions included: i) three online trainings for 50 constituents and members of the NTCDC in 2022 to increase their capacity to mainstream ILS (C102, C122, R202, R204 and social dialogue) in the two strategies ; ii) seven online webinars (February to June 2023) on integrated case management in social and employment sphere for 40 staff (30 % were women) of two Ministries and Agencies working on employment and social protection and regional employment and social protection services. They resulted in the development of a guide for the implementation of integrated case management; iii) methodology development and guidance for the Research Institute under the Ministry of Labour to conduct surveys on the adequacy of a minimum consumption basket and appropriateness of the methodology. The survey was validated by constituents and published in April 2023. ILO supported the Federation of Trade Unions during 5 sub-regional trainings for 100 members (October 2022 to March 2023) focusing on outreach to workers in the informal economy and extension of social protection. Key reports developed with or by constituents with ILO's support: the Public Expenditure and Institutional Review of the Social Protection System; Composition, Structure and Affordability of Minimum Consumption Basket; and Rapid Assessment of the Situation of Workers in Informal Economy.

description.narrative: The State Program on Productive Employment for 2023-2027 was approved by the Government of Tajikistan on 30 August 2023. The Programme covers active and passive measures to promote employment of the population, including provision of career guidance, organisation of job fairs, and referral of the unemployed to vocational training and paid public works. It stipulates unemployment benefits and employment quota for disadvantaged groups of workers. The programme is based on the priorities entailed in the National Development Strategy of the Republic of Tajikistan for the period up to 2030, and the Concept for the Development of Productive Employment of the Republic of Tajikistan for the period up to 2040. It guides state budget allocation and policy initiatives to address acute Decent Work deficit in the country. The ILO conducted labour market and economic analysis to inform the employment programme formulation so that employment policy initiatives are evidence based. The ILO also provided technical assistance to draft employment programme and supported stakeholder consultation.
